chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from some of our companions, from Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who presents his evidence to establish his right; is it upon him to be sworn an oath? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفَ: To be sworn an oath (passive form)

ai.seo_question: Is an oath required from the plaintiff after presenting evidence in Islamic court?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of *bayyinah* (clear evidence) is prioritized over the plaintiff's oath, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential principle that strong proof renders the oath superfluous. This ruling highlights the procedural efficiency in Islamic courts, where the weight of evidence supersedes the need for additional solemnization by the claimant, a stance distinct from some other schools where the oath may serve as a supplementary guarantee.
